ideas: Children's exposure to junk food adverts
Rising obesity and its cost to society
Freedom of businesses and personal choice

phrases.meaning: children nagging parents to buy things

phrases.phrase: a burden on the health system
phrases.meaning: heavy cost for hospitals and doctors

model: I believe fast food advertising should be restricted, especially when it targets children. First, kids can't really make informed choices, and companies know that. Adverts use cartoons and free toys to target children, and then pester power does the rest. My niece, for example, begs her parents for fried chicken every time she sees a certain advert on YouTube. So governments should ban junk food adverts during peak viewing hours and on children's channels, as some countries have already done. Another reason is that childhood obesity is rising quickly in many countries, including Vietnam, and overweight children often grow into adults with diabetes or heart problems. That becomes a burden on the health system that everyone has to pay for. Of course, a total ban would go too far, because adults are supposed to be free to decide what they eat, and restaurants have a right to advertise. But restricting adverts aimed at kids seems reasonable. So overall, yes, I think we ought to limit fast food marketing, at least for young audiences.
